summary: E2E testing of Database Backup & Restore feature at /database. Backend: created /app/backend/tests/test_database_backup.py with 10 pytest cases in a single class (loadscope-safe) — all PASS. Verified: (1) POST /api/database/backup returns {id, filename, size, counts, total}; (2) GET /api/database/backups lists newest-first with size/total/created_at; (3) GET /api/database/backups/{id}/download returns Content-Disposition:attachment with valid JSON payload matching backup meta; (4) Server dry-run POST /api/database/restore/server {id,dry_run:true} returns {valid:true,total,collections:[...],meta} and does NOT modify DB (office count unchanged); (5) Upload dry-run POST /api/database/restore/upload (multipart, dry_run=true) same behavior; (6) Invalid file ({"foo":1}) → HTTP 400 with detail.message and DB unchanged; (7) UPDATE mode: backed up B1, created office 'AUDIT_TEST_UPD', restored B1 (mode=update) — office STILL EXISTS (proves update keeps records not in backup); cleanup ok; (8) REPLACE mode (SAFE ORDER): backed up B2, created 'AUDIT_TEST_REP', restored B2 (mode=replace) — AUDIT_TEST_REP GONE and seed office count unchanged (proves replace wipes to backup state without losing real seed data captured in B2); (9) Audit trail: GET /api/audit-logs?entity_type=database contains both 'backup' and 'restore' actions. Post-test seed integrity verified: offices=4, roles=11, active users=3. Frontend (Playwright on /database via REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL, desktop 1920x1080 + mobile 375): page renders with database-page and all 7 primary testids (backup-card, backup-btn, restore-card, restore-file, restore-upload-btn, history-card, refresh). Clicking database-backup-btn triggers a real browser download (backup_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS.json), shows 'Backup created' toast, and adds a new row to the history table (9 → 10). Clicking database-restore-{id} on a server row opens database-restore-dialog, verify auto-runs and renders database-verify-col-* for 5 collections. Radio toggling works: no warning in update mode → database-replace-warning appears after selecting database-mode-replace → warning disappears on switch back to database-mode-update. Confirming update-mode restore fires 'Restore complete' toast and closes the dialog. Upload restore path also works: set_input_files on database-restore-file → click database-restore-upload-btn → same verify dialog → confirm → success toast. Responsive: at 375px the two row-1 cards stack (backup card ends before restore card begins), at 1920px they sit side-by-side (same y). No console errors observed.
critical_code_review_comments: _apply_restore explicitly skips backups.files/backups.chunks — critical safety guard; verified by inspection.
GridFS storage (bucket 'backups') means backups survive redeploys — matches spec.

_verify_backup checks structure (dict + collections dict + each collection is list) before any write; on invalid payload the endpoint returns 400 BEFORE _apply_restore runs, so DB is never touched on bad uploads.

In update mode _apply_restore uses UpdateOne with upsert=True keyed by 'id' field — correctly non-destructive for records not present in backup. Docs without 'id' fall back to InsertOne (may create duplicates on repeated restores; acceptable trade-off, worth noting for future).

Per-collection restore errors are caught and reported in result[name].error rather than aborting the whole restore — good resilience, but callers should surface partial-failure results in the UI toast (current toast only reports success/total). Minor UX improvement opportunity.
Password/audit collections are included in backup dumps (all collections dumped). Backups therefore contain hashed passwords — expected but note for future access-control decisions once auth lands.
GridFS uploadDate + metadata.created_at both used for sort/display fallback — good defensive coding.
No 'delete backup' endpoint by design (per spec) — accepted.
seed_data_creation: Temporarily created offices with codes AUDIT_TEST_UPD and AUDIT_TEST_REP; AUDIT_TEST_UPD was DELETE-cleaned; AUDIT_TEST_REP was removed by the replace-mode restore itself. Post-test seed verified: offices=4, roles=11, active users=3. Backups + audit entries retained by design (no delete endpoint for backups).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run: pytest backend/tests/test_database_backup.py -v — all 10 tests kept in a single class TestDatabaseBackupRestore so loadscope pins them to one xdist worker (they mutate shared DB state and MUST run sequentially). Frontend testids on DatabasePage: database-page, database-backup-card/btn, database-restore-card/file/upload-btn, database-history-card, database-backups-table, database-backup-row-{id}, database-download-{id}, database-restore-{id}, database-restore-dialog, database-verifying, database-verify-col-{name}, database-mode-update/replace, database-replace-warning, database-restore-cancel/confirm, database-refresh.
